changelog: Replace C2 severity to mark splitting multi-word personal names or separating a name from its immediately following appositive/title as especially severe — to give the model a severity axis that orders cuts inside names in line with the measured target.
findings: When multiple candidate cuts all lie inside the same multi-word personal name the prompt ranks them inconsistently; the better choice is the cut that leaves the whole name unbroken in one piece.
The prompt allows cuts that split multi-word personal names or separate a name from its immediately following appositive/title, which breaks cohesion and harms translation of the whole sentence.

diagnosis.why: Making cuts inside multi-word personal names or name+appositive especially severe caused the model to avoid splitting names (helping mid-length budgets: ≤5 and ≤7 showed small gains) but it also re-ranked the very top candidate cut positions (rank_depth 1..3 all fell), so for the shortest latency bins (≤3) the prompt now prefers earlier, worse splits of nearby noun phrases and determiners and H_set dropped there.
diagnosis.lesson: When increasing severity for name-internal cuts, ensure the change does not re-rank the first one or two candidate cuts (short-latency depths), since that can force harmful early splits of adjacent noun phrases/determiners and degrade short-bin performance.
